$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: A Map with a Missing Pass

plate.narration: Outside the singing hall, packs rest beside a waiting sledge. Beyond its sheltered ledge, white paths disappear between the peaks. There is room on the map for more than one road.

goal.text: Meet the travelers and get ready for the road ahead.

map.narration: The griffin calls to the unicorn. "Olivia. Your hoof." She steps aside. He folds his map, finds another corner stuck under a bag, and gives up. "Good morning. I'm Orin Vale." "Lady Olivia," the unicorn adds. Behind them, a kitsune tightens a strap on a case of small rings. "Seren Wisp," she says, waving. An open case of little brass instruments rests beside Orin's pack. "Were you the noise over the ridge?" he asks. Your job today: meet these travelers, help them pack, and get ready for the road ahead.

choices.label: Tell them how you arrived
Ask whether they saw the fold

arrival_story.narration: You tell Orin about the snow, the kid, and the quay vanishing behind you. He writes down "goat" and underlines it. "A place arrived first. Then you crossed." Olivia leans over his shoulder. "And it reached all the way here."

choices.label: Ask who they are

arrival_question.narration: "We saw it close," says Seren. She checks that everyone is standing steady. "You all came through together? Good." Orin opens his notebook. Olivia is watching the slope where the fold closed.

choices.label: Ask what they are doing here

fellowship.narration: "Riftseekers," says Orin, touching the broken-circle clasp on his cloak. "We call these openings rifts. We follow them and write down what they do." "Some of us would like to do more than write," says Lady Olivia. Seren closes her ring case. "Some of us would like to arrive with all our luggage." Beside them, the travelers' sledge leans like a sleepy goat. Orin frowns at it. "We leave when it stops leaning. Hands would help."

choices.label: Lift the trunks onto the sledge together
Use brace to hold the leaning sledge steady
Smash the ice off the sledge runners

sledge_lift.narration: Four trunks, three sacks, a crate of notebooks and a barrel that sloshes. Olivia points with one hoof. "Heavy things low, light things high." Orin has drawn a diagram on his sleeve. "Hand to hand," he says. "Nobody carries the whole pile."

interaction.cue: Catch each trunk and pass it along to the sledge.

onSuccess.narration: Up it all goes, hand to hand. The sledge stops leaning and sits level as a loaf. Olivia lifts the lid of a small clay jar to check it. "Mosslight, for the road. You earned it." The moss inside glows like a sleepy star.

onFailure.narration: The barrel goes up faster than the trunks, and everything meets in the middle. A sack of oats bursts. Olivia hops over it with great dignity. You restack the load, but the sledge keeps its lean.

onAssisted.narration: Orin steadies the chain with a long pole, and the trunks glide along. The sledge sits level as a loaf. Olivia lifts the lid of a small clay jar to check it. "Mosslight, for the road. You earned it." The moss inside glows like a sleepy star.

sledge_brace.narration: Brace is a stout sort of magic: plant your feet and become a wall. You set a shoulder to the sledge while the others lift.
sledge_brace.prompt: Hold the sledge steady while the heavy trunks go on.

onSuccess.narration: Not one runner wobbles. The trunks settle in with soft thumps, and the sledge sits level as a loaf. Olivia lifts the lid of a small clay jar to check it. "Mosslight, for the road. You earned it." The moss inside glows like a sleepy star.

onFailure.narration: The barrel goes up faster than the trunks, and everything meets in the middle. A sack of oats bursts. Olivia hops over it with great dignity. You restack the load, but the sledge keeps its lean.

sledge_smash.narration: A crust of old ice holds the sledge runners like a hand. Smash is a good answer to a crust.
sledge_smash.prompt: Smash the ice off the runners, then shove the sledge level.

onSuccess.narration: Crack! The ice flies off in a shower of glitter, and the sledge rocks upright. Everyone pats the trunks into place. Olivia lifts the lid of a small clay jar to check it. "Mosslight, for the road. You earned it." The moss inside glows like a sleepy star.

onFailure.narration: The barrel goes up faster than the trunks, and everything meets in the middle. A sack of oats bursts. Olivia hops over it with great dignity. You restack the load, but the sledge keeps its lean.

ring_sort.narration: Seren sets her ring case on a flat stone and lifts the lid. Rings of every size lie inside, each with its own tiny hum. The rush has jostled them. "They go back in order," she says, "or the lid will not close, and the lid is all that keeps them from singing in my pack all night." She hands out little cards. "Each card knows something. Share what yours says."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then put the rings in order.
clues: The low ring goes in first.
The high ring goes right before the middle ring.

onSuccess.narration: Click, click, click. The last ring drops in with a note like a dropped spoon. Seren blinks. "Hm. You are better at this than Orin." The lid closes with a satisfied sigh.

onFailure.narration: Two rings land in the wrong grooves. The lid closes anyway, and the case hums a little crooked. Seren sighs fondly. "I will fix it by the fire. Rings are patient."

onAssisted.narration: You lay every card side by side. Low, high, middle. The lid closes with a satisfied sigh, and Seren tucks the case under her arm.

seren.narration: Seren asks where the opening appeared and how long it lasted. She listens without interrupting. Orin rolls the map around a wooden rod so nobody can stand on it again.

choices.label: Help Orin with his instruments

variants.text: When you describe studying the light around the opening, Seren looks up. "One of you can see it. Keep looking. Later, I can show you how to listen too."
"You can learn a good deal without seeing what I see," Seren says. She glances at Orin's instruments. "He brought half a bag of help."

instruments.narration: Orin opens the case of little brass instruments. Frost has crept into every hinge. A horn whines. A tiny trumpet will not move at all. "The best ears should find the flat one," he says, "and the best fingers should fix it. I have no idea who has which." The flat one is the little trumpet. A drop of warm tea in its hinge, a twist, and it sings true. Orin holds it to his ear like a shell. "Better than new," he tells Seren. Seren says that is not possible, and smiles.

choices.label: Continue together

corner_hunt.narration: Orin pats his coat, his bag, his hat. "My map is still pinned under the load," he says. "If it tears, the pass tears with it." He looks at you hopefully. Trunks are heavy, and paper is not. Slip, slide, free. The map comes out whole and flat. Orin hugs it, then remembers himself and only pats it. "Thank you. I would have drawn the pass in the wrong place forever."

choices.label: Continue together

lead.narration: Orin unrolls his map and points east. "The griffins at Frostfang keep a ledger of their passes. Last season, no pass here. This season, cairns and a path. They call it the Cairnstep." He marks the herder's flooded grazing route beside it. "If the pass reaches this bank, supplies could get through to the herd. It might also show us why a road no longer leads where people expect. We need to find where it really goes."

choices.label: Ask what they would do first

olivia.narration: Olivia taps the flooded route on the map. "There is food in my pack. If we could carry it through an opening, the herd could eat today." Orin lifts his own pack. "I will carry food. But I will not send someone into a rift before we know whether they can return." Seren watches your faces. "What would you put first?"

choices.label: Help the people waiting now
Find safe routes for the next travelers

help_now.narration: Olivia takes a supper bundle from her pack and calls the herder over. "This much can go by hand." Orin makes room for it on the sledge. "And we can learn the route before we send more." Seren nods to you. "A useful place to begin."

choices.label: Pull the sledge to the herder's tent

safe_routes.narration: Orin draws a careful line beside the Cairnstep. "A route people can trust. Yes." Olivia leaves a supper bundle for the herder. "We can feed someone while you check it." Seren looks at the glacier. "And listen here, if the road is not the question you want to follow."

choices.label: Mark the safe bank for Orin

haul_supper.narration: The herder's tent stands across a yard of slick, packed ice. The supper has to get there warm, and the sledge has to get there upright.
haul_supper.prompt: Steer the sledge around the slick patches to the herder's tent.

onSuccess.narration: The sledge glides like a duck on a pond. The herder lifts the lid, sniffs, and closes her eyes. "Warm." Orin taps a flat tin on his belt, the Riftseekers' helper fund. "Everyone who hauls gets paid." Four coins clink into your hands, and the herder slips you a honeycake too.

onFailure.narration: The sledge hits glare ice and spins once, slowly, with everyone's dignity. The supper arrives a little shaken, and the goats rush over to check it. The herder laughs into her sleeve. Orin counts two coins from a flat tin, the Riftseekers' helper fund. "For effort."

chalk_route.narration: Orin hands you a stick of chalk and his longest list of questions. Which stones sit steady? Which snow hangs over an edge? The herder watches from her tent door. "Mark the bank where my goats walk," she says, "and mark it right."
chalk_route.prompt: Walk the bank beside the hall and chalk every steady stone.

onSuccess.narration: Your chalk runs straight along the bank, steady stone to steady stone. Orin traces it with a finger. "A route people can trust." He taps a flat tin on his belt, the Riftseekers' helper fund, and counts four coins into your hand. The herder sends over a warm honeycake.

onFailure.narration: Your chalk marks one stone wrong, and a goat points it out by sitting on it. It skids. You rub out the mark and try the next stone. Orin counts two coins from a flat tin, the Riftseekers' helper fund. "For honesty."

route.narration: Orin points below the ice shelf, where melt channels join into a broad river. "The Great River starts here. Stay on this bank. The shelf above the headwaters leads toward Frostfang. Test the ice. If it gives, let the river carry you to a place you can get out. Do not fight it under the shelf." Seren points toward the hall. "Or study the seam that answered your song. Look for signs of openings around the glacier. Learning what they need might help you find a way home." Orin traces a longer road above the bank. "Or follow these markers to a ferry at a place called Ashspan Bridge. It takes longer, but it stays off the ice. From the bridge, an upper bank road goes back north to Frostfang Shore."

choices.label: Look over the river for yourselves

lookout.narration: From the ledge by the hall you can see how the land lies. Melt channels braid down toward the Great River. Above them, the ice shelf shines. Orin hands you his spyglass, then takes it back to find which end is the right end. "Look first," he says. "Then walk." How will you look?

choices.label: Climb the rock stair to the high ledge
Read the clouds and wind from where you stand
Take to your wings for a better look

lookout_climb.narration: The rock stair is a rumor of steps, glued together with frost.
lookout_climb.prompt: Climb to the high ledge without losing a boot.

onSuccess.narration: From the ledge the river lies below like a long silver ribbon. The ice shelf above it has one dark patch where the surface looks thin. You hold on tight and remember where.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up, a step turns out to be a rumor. You slide back down and land in a soft drift. From the bottom you can still see the shelf, but only most of it.

lookout_sky.narration: Wind tells you what the ice is doing, if you watch the snow it drags.
lookout_sky.prompt: Watch the drifting snow and the clouds, and work out where the air is coming from.

onSuccess.narration: The snow streams off one place on the shelf faster than anywhere else. That patch is thin, or hollow, or both. You keep it in your head.

onFailure.narration: The clouds say rain, snow, or nothing at all. You decide the sky is being mysterious on purpose.

lookout_fly.narration: Wings make a lookout easy, if the wind agrees. One of you rises, and the others call up what to find.
lookout_fly.prompt: Fly a slow circle over the shelf and read the ice from above.

onSuccess.narration: From above, the whole shelf lies flat like a map. One dark patch shows where the ice is thin. You land and point at it before you forget.

onFailure.narration: A gust flips you sideways. You flutter down laughing, with snow in your feathers and a lot of sky in your eyes.

sketch.narration: Orin unrolls his map beside the sledge and hands you his pencil. "Draw what you saw," he says. "Maps are made by whoever looked last." Seren props a corner with a rock. What do you add?

choices.label: Draw the ice shelf and its edge
Draw the river's first bend
Draw the singing hall and its sealed seam

sketch_shelf.narration: You draw the shelf as a long white tongue above the river, edges wobbling. Orin leans in. "Wobbly and true beats neat and wrong," he says. Olivia lifts her nose. "Wind is coming," she says. "Hold the cover!"

choices.label: Hold the cover

variants.text: You add a small dark patch where the ice looked thin. Orin circles it twice.

sketch_bend.narration: You draw the river's first bend, where the melt channels pour in. Seren taps the bend. "Loud water hides small sounds," she says. "Remember that." Olivia lifts her nose. "Wind is coming," she says. "Hold the cover!"

choices.label: Hold the cover

sketch_hall.narration: You draw the singing hall and the sealed seam behind it. Orin says nothing for a moment. Then he writes "ASK" beside it, very small. "That is a question worth a trip," he says. Olivia lifts her nose. "Wind is coming," she says. "Hold the cover!"

choices.label: Hold the cover

tarp.narration: The gust arrives, cold and rude. It slides under the sledge cover and lifts it like a big white sail.

variants.text: The leaning sledge catches the wind like a sail, too.

tarp.prompt: Everyone grab a corner and tie the cover down before it flies!

onSuccess.narration: Knot, knot, knot. The cover snaps once, then lies down like a tired dog. Olivia checks every knot and, to her own surprise, finds nothing to fix.

onFailure.narration: The cover escapes with a slap and flaps across the yard like a fat white bird. You chase it into a drift and drag it back. Everyone is cold, and somebody has a bruised elbow.

tea.narration: Seren builds a small stove from a tin and a candle in the lee of the sledge. Steam fogs Orin's spectacles at once. He leaves them fogged. "Hands first," says Seren. "Questions after." You sit in a row on the trunks. Whose story do you ask for while the tea warms?

choices.label: Ask Seren how she first met a rift
Ask Olivia what she wants rifts for

tea_seren.narration: Seren holds her cup in both paws. "A hum like a kettle, behind a barn. I followed it in my slippers." She sips. "Never follow a kettle in slippers. Bring boots. Bring somebody who will pull you back."

choices.label: Pass the cups along

tea_olivia.narration: Olivia swirls her tea. "A door that opens by itself? I would like to know whose hand is on it, and whether I could borrow it for the herd." She winks. Orin coughs into his mug. "Ask. Do not borrow." "I always ask," says Olivia. "Loudly."

choices.label: Pass the cups along

supplies.narration: Seren props open the lid of a battered tin on the sledge. Inside lie spare things for the road: a coil of cord, a very small spoon, and a brass whistle on a loop. "Fair swaps," she says. "A brave whistle costs three coins." Behind the sledge, the herder's goats are chewing the tow rope again, and they look hungry. What do you do with your last minutes here?

choices.label: Buy the brave whistle for 3 coins
Share a supper with the hungry goats
Tighten every knot on the sledge ropes
Rub tallow on the sledge runners

supplies_buy.narration: Three coins clink into Seren's tin. She hands over the whistle. "One loud note," she says. "Use it when you need to be heard, not when you want to be."

choices.label: Take the chime from Orin

supplies_feed.narration: The goats bundle around you, soft noses everywhere. The herder pulls a river charm from her coat and presses it into your hand. "I found it in a melt channel," she says. "It likes people who share."

choices.label: Take the chime from Orin

supplies_tight.narration: You check every knot twice and tug the lashings tight. The sledge stops creaking. Seren nods at the ropes. "The best spare is a good knot."

choices.label: Take the chime from Orin

supplies_oil.narration: The tallow smells like warm candles. You rub it into the runners until they shine. The sledge slides forward at a nudge, and Olivia has to catch it by the tail.

choices.label: Take the chime from Orin

chime.narration: Orin takes a little chime from his bag. "A Listening Chime, for you. Strike it near an opening. A sour note means it cannot open yet. An echo means it will stay open and let you come back." He waits while you take it. "No echo? Do not promise anybody a return trip. Away from a rift, it is only a very small bell."

choices.label: Try the Listening Chime

test_chime.narration: The Listening Chime hangs from a short cord. It is light enough to carry in one hand. Orin holds his bag open while you decide how to test it.

choices.label: Ring it beside the empty air
Wrap it carefully and repeat the rules
Hold the mosslight jar close and look at the chime
Blow the brave whistle and see if it answers

ring.narration: You strike it. One clear note rings over the snow and fades. No opening answers. Orin nods. "See? A very small bell." Seren smiles. "Still worth keeping."

choices.label: Get ready for Seren's practice

wrap.narration: "Sour: not ready. Echo: a way back," you say. Orin nods and gives you a scrap of soft cloth for the chime. "And never ask it for the name of a place. It does not know the names."

choices.label: Pack the chime

chime_jar.narration: You hold the jar close. The moss glows soft and warm, and the chime throws a shivery shadow across the snow. Seren smiles. "Now you know where it hangs in the dark. Useful." Orin writes in his notebook: "Chime, visible by lamplight."

choices.label: Get ready for Seren's practice

chime_whistle.narration: You blow the brave whistle. One loud note rolls over the camp, and every goat looks up. The chime does not answer at all. "It does not take orders from whistles," says Orin. "Good. That would be a very bossy chime."

choices.label: Get ready for Seren's practice

trial_intro.narration: Seren sets three rings on a flat stone and turns her back. Olivia flaps a blanket to make wind. Orin plays one squeaky note on his horn. "Training," says Seren. "A rift will not be quiet for you. Two of these rings ring true. One rings sour. If you can hear it through all this noise, you can hear it anywhere."

choices.label: Listen to the rings

trial_read.narration: The three rings sit in a row on the stone. The blanket flaps. The horn squeaks. Which ring is sour, and how will you find out?

choices.label: Close your eyes and listen past the noise
Hold your chime beside each ring and compare
Use rally to hum each ring's note back

trial_ear.narration: You shut your eyes. The blanket flaps, the horn squeaks, and under it all, three rings hum.
trial_ear.prompt: Pick out the sour ring through the flapping and squeaking.

onSuccess.narration: You point at the middle ring. Seren's ears twitch, which means yes.

onFailure.narration: You point at the first ring. It is true, and it says so, loudly.

trial_chime.narration: Here the chime is only a bell. It is a bell with a good ear for company, though. It rings sweet beside a true ring, and it buzzes beside a flawed one.
trial_chime.prompt: Swing the chime beside each ring, one after another, before Olivia flaps the blanket again.

onSuccess.narration: You point at the middle ring. Seren's ears twitch, which means yes.

onFailure.narration: You point at the first ring. It is true, and it says so, loudly.

trial_hum.narration: Rally listens before it sings. You hum a low note and wait to see which ring hums back kindly, and which one hums back crooked.
trial_hum.prompt: Hum to each ring and hear which one answers wrong.

onSuccess.narration: You point at the middle ring. Seren's ears twitch, which means yes.

onFailure.narration: You point at the first ring. It is true, and it says so, loudly.

trial_report.narration: Seren turns back around. "The sour one was the middle ring," she says. "A rift gives the same warning: one wrong note among right ones. Hear it, and you do not walk in. Hear the echo, and it will keep a door open behind you." Orin writes that down, then crosses it out. "Too wordy."

choices.label: Echo her pattern

trial_echo.narration: Seren holds up one paw, and the blanket goes still. She taps the three rings in a pattern, slow and clear. Orin leans in. Olivia stops breathing, which for Olivia is a lot.

interaction.cue: Watch Seren tap the rings, then tap the same rings in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Low, high, middle, low. Seren's ears twitch twice, which means yes. "An echo is only a pattern that remembers itself," she says.

onFailure.narration: Your echo comes out a little jumbled. Seren taps it once more, slowly, and you hear where it wandered off.

onAssisted.narration: Seren taps the pattern again while Orin hums it under his breath. Low, high, middle, low. This time it sticks.

trial_all.narration: Seren shuffles the rings behind her back, then strikes one. Olivia flaps the blanket harder. Orin plays his squeaky note with great pride. Every finger points the same way. Seren strikes the ring again to check, and the sour note proves you right. Olivia salutes with the blanket.

choices.label: Continue together

prep.narration: The sledge is packed. The practice is done. Orin taps the ice shelf on the rolled-up map. Seren glances back at the singing hall. "Two roads are worth walking ready," she says. "The shelf toward the Cairnstep, with food for the herd, or the glacier, looking for openings. There is also the long bank road to Ashspan Bridge, if you would rather stay off the ice." Which road do you get ready for?

choices.label: Practice testing ice for the shelf
Practice listening at the glacier wall with Seren
Walk the first markers of the long bank road
Scout the bank road at a run
Light the mosslight jar and read the glacier wall

prep_ice.narration: Orin lays a slab of old ice on the snow. "Thick ice rings when you tap it," he says. "Thin ice thuds." He hands you a stone. "Stamp, tap, listen." Ring, ring, thud! You find the thin spot with one tap. Orin cheers very quietly, so as not to wake the ice.

variants.text: You remember the dark patch you saw from the ledge. It will probably thud.

choices.label: Continue together

prep_seam.narration: Seren leads you along the glacier wall behind the hall and presses an ear to the ice. "Listen for a tick," she says. "Listen for a hum. Listen for a quiet that is too tidy." You find the spot where the sealed seam's hum is clearest and mark it with a pebble. Seren nods. "A hum that holds still can be learned."

choices.label: Continue together

prep_jar.narration: With the mosslight jar held up, the glacier wall glows from inside, as if the ice were a lantern. Frost patterns bloom across it like ferns. One frost line runs straight to the sealed seam and stops. "Look at that," says Seren. "The ice remembers where the seam is."

choices.label: Continue together

prep_bank.narration: A line of little stone markers runs away along the bank, each one a neat heap. Some have tipped over in the wind. Every marker stands straight again, and the road to the bridge looks friendlier. Orin ticks something off in his notebook.

choices.label: Continue together

prep_dash.narration: A duskrunner's feet know the quiet way. One of you takes off along the bank road, light and fast, while the others watch from the sledge. You come back breathless, with the road clear in your head: no gaps, no drifts, only a goat on a rock. Orin writes down "goat on rock."

choices.label: Continue together

parting.narration: Olivia shoulders her pack. Seren counts the cases once, then again. Orin takes the path behind them, holding the map up where everyone can see it. "If the Cairnstep has moved," he calls back, "do draw it in the right place."

choices.label: Choose your next direction

variants.text: The sledge still leans a little. Olivia pats it. "Character," she says.

camp_play.narration: The Riftseekers are gone down the path. The herder's goats wander over to the sledge, and the yetis lean out of the hall door. Nobody says goodbye to a road without a proper send-off.

interaction.cue: Give the goats and the hall a proper send-off.

options.label: Hum the low note
options.reaction: The hall hums back, low and warm.

options.label: Pet a goat
options.reaction: A goat leans its whole weight against your knees.

options.label: Cheer for the road
options.reaction: Every goat looks up, then goes back to chewing the tow rope.

onSuccess.narration: The low note rolls out of the hall, and the goats hum along in their own way. The herder waves, and her kid goat tries to wave too.

onFailure.narration: The goats are busy with the tow rope, and the yetis are busy with a very long note. You wave anyway.

camp.narration: You sit on a dry stone beside the singing hall. East, the ice shelf leads toward the Cairnstep: perhaps a supply route for the herd, if the shifting ice lets you reach it. Behind you, the sealed seam answered your song. Exploring the glacier might teach you how to find another opening. The Listening Chime rests between you. Safe roads for the people already here, or a better understanding of the openings that brought you? Your party has something to talk about before setting out. A longer marked bank road leads to Ashspan Bridge without crossing the ice shelf.

choices.label: Talk it over and set out
Eat a proper supper together
Look back at the singing hall

camp_supper.narration: You split the food on the dry stone, crumb by crumb. It is warm, and it tastes like a good decision. The Listening Chime swings gently between you, as if it is licking its lips.

choices.label: Talk it over and set out

camp_hall.narration: Through the hall door, a yeti hums the low note you learned. It rises to meet you, then fades. The hall will keep your note until you come back to sing it.

choices.label: Talk it over and set out

set_out.narration: You brush the snow off your packs and stand. Inside the hall, the yetis hold their low note a little longer, as if they are waving. The shelf, the glacier openings, or the long bank road to the bridge: which road comes first?

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Orin Vale: He/him, griffin Riftseeker. Methodical, patient, plain speech, asks questions instead of explaining the world. Offers one optional practical lead; no Pangea theory yet.
npcVoices.Lady Olivia: She/her, unicorn Riftseeker. Confident, mischievous, sees useful possibilities in rifts. Wants power to help, no threats and no early summoning.
npcVoices.Seren Wisp: She/her, kitsune Riftseeker. Careful, perceptive, kind. Recognizes an earlier Starweaver reading by its flag. Promises teaching later; does not grant Attune here.

listening_chime.name: Listening Chime
listening_chime.text: Near a rift: sour means not ready; an echo means it stays open and offers a way back.
